newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak NBS sets 45-wk T-bill auction on Wed.
newsitem.headline: Slovak NBS sets 45-wk T-bill auction on Wed.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia will auction an unspecified tranche of 45-week finance ministry treasury bills on Wednesday, July 30, the central bank (NBS) said.
The T-bills will have the longest maturity so far this year. A tranch of 26-week T-bills were sold on May 22 at an average yield of 14.25 percent.
Last week the Finance Ministry accepted an average yield of 17.80 percent in an auction of one-year state bonds.
The ministry does not set an amount on offer in state securities auctions, nor does it set a minimum or maximum limit price on bids.

It uses T-bills and state bonds as the main tools to cover the state budget deficit, which widened to 17.790 billion crowns as of July 8, 1997, from 7.177 billion crowns in the January-May period of 1997.
